input.description: Find call sites of startBackgroundRunners, AllowPrivateIPs, ValidateURL

content.text:
All findings confirmed. Here are the answers.

## h01: S3 presigned URL refresh runner

**Component:** `server/runner/s3presign` — the `Runner` in `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`. It re-presigns S3-stored attachment references so external links don't expire.

**Schedule:**
- Interval constant: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` — `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (comment on line 26: "Schedule runner every 12 hours").
- `Run` loop with ticker: lines 29–41 — `ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)` at line 30, firing `r.RunOnce(ctx)` at line 36 until `ctx.Done()`.
- `RunOnce`: lines 43–45, which calls `CheckAndPresign` (line 47). That method pages attachments with `StorageType == S3` in batches of 100, skips ones presigned within the last ~4 days (URL lifetime is 5 days; skip check at line 88), and calls `s3Client.PresignGetObject` (line 108), then persists the new URL via `UpdateAttachment` with `Reference: &presignURL` (lines 116–119) and stamps `LastPresignedTime` (line 115).

**Startup wiring** in `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`:
- `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` called from `Server.Start` at **server/server.go:129**.
- Inside `startBackgroundRunners` (line 153): runner created at **server/server.go:162** (`s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)`), an immediate synchronous pass `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` at **line 163**, then the continuous loop launched in a goroutine `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` at **line 169** (with a dedicated cancellable context created at line 156 and WaitGroup tracking at line 166).

## h02: Webhook HTTP delivery and SSRF protection

**Delivery function:** `Post` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go` (lines 120–180). The request is built with `http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, ...)` at **internal/webhook/webhook.go:126** and actually executed at **internal/webhook/webhook.go:152** via `resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)`. Async dispatch goes through `PostAsync` (line 184) into a bounded queue drained by 4 workers (init, lines 42–55) that call the same `Post`.

**SSRF protections — two layers:**

1. **Dial-time IP blocking (defeats DNS rebinding):** `safeClient` (webhook.go:32–37) is an `http.Client` whose Transport uses `safeDialContext` (webhook.go:59–77). At connection time it resolves the hostname (line 65) and rejects any resolved address in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` (check at lines 70–74). Because this happens at dial time on every request, a hostname that passed validation earlier but later resolves to an internal IP is still blocked.

2. **Registration-time URL validation:** `ValidateURL` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go:62–83` — requires an absolute http/https URL (scheme check line 67), resolves the hostname (line 71), and rejects reserved/private IPs (lines 76–81), returning gRPC `InvalidArgument`. Called when webhooks are created/updated in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` at lines 74, 161, and 182.

The blocklist `reservedCIDRs` (validate.go:14–23) covers IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.0/8, RFC-1918 (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local 169.254.0.0/16 (explicitly including cloud IMDS 169.254.169.254), plus IPv6 ::1/128, fc00::/7, fe80::/10. There is an escape hatch `AllowPrivateIPs` (validate.go:41, checked in `isReservedIP` at line 45) for self-hosted deployments — grep shows it is never set anywhere in non-test code, so protection is effectively always on. Additional hardening in `Post`: 30s client timeout (webhook.go:27) and a 1 MiB response body cap via `io.LimitReader` (webhook.go:158). Requests can also carry a Standard-Webhooks HMAC-SHA256 signature (webhook.go:133–150), which is integrity/authenticity, not SSRF-related.
